text:
ConocoPhillips inched down today after climbing 5.3% over the past two weeks—a move that reflects conflicting pressures on oil and fuel markets. The stock has been buoyed by a sharp rise in crude prices (US oil at $96/barrel, global oil at $125/barrel) driven by ongoing supply disruptions from tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, hurricane damage to Gulf of Mexico production, and refinery losses from wars in Eastern Europe and the Middle East. Today's near-flat close suggests the market is weighing that tailwind against the news that Trump has struck a deal with Putin to supply Russian diesel to U.S. and global markets—a move that could ease the fuel shortage pressuring prices upward, at least modestly.

The diesel deal introduces uncertainty for integrated oil producers like ConocoPhillips. While higher crude prices support their upstream operations, a flow of Russian diesel into global markets could dampen the refining margins and fuel scarcity premiums that have been a windfall for U.S. refiners facing destruction of capacity abroad. The geopolitical risk remains volatile—tanker attacks and hurricane impacts could quickly overwhelm any relief from the Russian deal.
